A stack of layers of [[Neuron|neurons]], fitted to data. See [[MACHINE LEARNING]] for the course
index and [[Multilayer Perceptron]] for the standard architecture; what this note carries is the
**training loop**, which is the one thing that ties every other note in the folder together.

## The loop

Five steps, repeated until the loss stops improving:

1. **Initialise** the [[Weights]] small and random, [[Bias Term|biases]] at zero.
2. **[[Forward Pass]]**: push a batch of inputs through, layer by layer, to get predictions.
3. **[[Loss Function]]**: compare predictions against the true labels, get one number.
4. **[[Back Propagation]]**: [[Chain Rule]] backwards through the layers to get
   $\partial L / \partial w$ for every weight at once.
5. **[[Gradient Descent]]**: step every weight against its gradient, scaled by the learning rate.

Steps 2 to 5 over one batch is an *iteration*; a pass over the whole dataset is an *epoch*.
[[SGD Classification]] is the version where step 2 uses a random minibatch rather than everything,
which is what is actually run.

## Parameters versus hyperparameters

The distinction that decides what training can and cannot fix:

| | Chosen by | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Parameters** | gradient descent, during training | [[Weights]], [[Bias Term\|biases]] |
| **Hyperparameters** | you, before training | layer count and widths, which [[Activation Function]], learning rate, batch size |

A bad hyperparameter cannot be trained away. This is why the loop above sits inside an outer loop
of you changing numbers and rerunning it.

## Why it works at all

Nothing here is new mathematics. A [[Forward Pass]] is [[Matrix Multiplication]], the training
criterion is [[Optimization]] with a great many variables, and the gradient is the [[Chain Rule]].
What a network adds is a model family flexible enough that fitting it is worth the trouble, and
[[Non-Linear|non-linearity]] is the whole of that flexibility: without it the stack collapses to a
single linear map and the entire apparatus reduces to [[Linear Regression]].
